Locomotion is left at the existing 'Legged' value but is not maker-stated: it follows from the maker calling it a humanoid and from press breakdowns of the joints, so it should be treated as unconfirmed until a maker source or footage shows it moving. name: HRP-4C

Locomotion left null: the maker states autonomous movement but not the drive type, and no datasheet is published. Not related to CASBOT despite similar names (some aggregators conflate them). Launched Aug 19, 2025; mass production from June 16, 2026.

name: Xiaoan

summary: Open-source, 3D-printed 92 cm child-sized research humanoid with 20 Dynamixel actuators and ROS software, built by Uni Bonn's AIS group with igus.

name: FEDOR (Skybot F-850)

Nascent maker technical listings give 182 cm, 106 kg, 48 electromechanical drives, shoulder width 48 cm, about 1 h of continuous operation and walking speed about 4 km/h (1.11 m/s), Linux-based real-time OS; the ISS flight configuration is separately reported as 184 cm / 105 kg with 6 DOF per gripper and 10 kg per arm. CONFLICT recorded: press accounts of the 2019 flight give 160 kg for the ground model, so the weight depends on configuration; 106 kg is the maker listing figure. The legs were disabled in microgravity and the robot was teleoperated or ran predefined programs, so it is a research/demonstrator platform, never sold. No maker datasheet exists today - npo-at.com carries only news, so official_url points to the maker's FEDOR news item, and the 48 drives / 4 km/h / 1 h / 106 kg block is the most cited compilation of FEDOR listings (crediting Android Technics material), not a maker PDF. These figures are the least certain in this record.

Height 58 cm, width 27 cm, length 19 cm, mass 7 kg and 38 DOF (neck 4, waist 2, 5 per arm, 6 per leg, 5 independent fingers per hand) are the SDR-4XII figures published in the maker-side technical literature (Nagasaka, Sony, in Humanoid Robotics: A Reference). No height, weight, payload, speed, DOF, battery or runtime figures are published, so all spec fields stay empty. Maker timeline on its own site: whole robot assembled June 2026, multi-task demos summer 2026.

name: IGRIS-MAX
summary: ROBROS' next-generation bipedal industrial humanoid, announced 2026-11-04, built around stronger shoulder joints to carry loads of up to 30 kg.
note: Only maker material is the 2026-11-04 launch announcement ('Introducing IGRIS-MAX. More power. Greater possibilities', ROBROS LinkedIn and YouTube launch film 'Built for More'), which states a carrying capacity of up to 30 kg enabled by increased shoulder joint torque, aimed at heavier industrial handling. ROBROS' website still lists only IGRIS-C under Humanoid, and no datasheet, dimensions, weight, DOF, battery, speed or price has been published, so those fields stay empty. The 30 kg is a maker claim shown as a chest-held load in a film; it has not been independently tested, and no duration or walking condition is given.

Payload entered as the per-arm figure; the maker publishes no whole-robot payload.

name: Green
summary: Sber's Green humanoid from the Sber Robotics Center: a 180 cm, 41-DOF bipedal robot driven by GigaChat, demonstrated at AI Journey 2025 for kitting, sorting and lab-sample handling.
note: Maker page (sber.ru/robocenter/green) gives 180 cm, 75 kg and 41 degrees of freedom, and lists the demonstrated skills (spatial orientation, simple tasks, self-correction, natural-language speech through GigaChat) and target work (kitting and packing, test tubes and biological samples). Additional maker-disclosed figures from Sber's own technical presentation, reported 2025-11-21: 0.9 m/s, 8 RGB cameras + 2 LiDAR, 48 V battery, 1 CPU + 2 GPU compute, Ethernet and CAN-FD onboard network, force-torque fingers and inertial modules; the maker page's speed tile does not render a value for us, so the 0.9 m/s comes from that disclosure report. Presented at AI Journey on 2025-11-20/21; Sber said Green would be integrated into business processes soon, hence Pilot. No DOF breakdown, payload or runtime is published.

name: iLoabot-X
summary: Senad's heavy-duty wheeled dual-arm humanoid for the last 20 m of industrial logistics: 46 kg dual-arm load, a 0-2 m lifting column and a VLA logistics model for loading, palletizing and sorting.
note: Maker product brochure (Oct 2026) and product page: size 852 mm (upper body) / 700 mm (chassis) x 800 mm x 1,850 mm with 0-2 m dynamic lift, net weight 250-300 kg (entered as the 275 kg midpoint of the maker's range), 22 DOF (8 per arm x 2, torso 1, head 2, chassis 3), payload 46 kg with both arms (clamp/grip: 23 kg rated and 35 kg momentary per arm; suction: 12 kg rated per arm), max forward reach 955 mm and max arm span 2,060 mm, 0-2 m/s in the plant with a 1.2 m/s safety limit, 48 V / 6 kWh battery (=6,000 Wh) with 12 h continuous operation, 2.5 h charge and hot-swappable packs, -10 to 55 C, vision + LiDAR + force + pose fusion with 8 vision sensors, 3 LiDAR, UWB, IMU and 2 six-axis force sensors, quick-change gripper and suction end effectors. First shown at WRC 2025 in August 2025.

name: Linglong L1
summary: Linglong L1, the low-cost biped research platform of the National and Local Co-built Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (Shanghai).
note: Maker is Humanoid Robot (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., which operates the National and Local Co-built Humanoid Robot Innovation Center and the OpenLoong community (openloong.net). Its WRC 2026 exhibit entry describes L1 as a biped platform for general light-load work, built for legged-locomotion research and for validating embodied algorithms on 7-DoF humanoid arms, with low cost, high compatibility and modularity as the selling points; the entry publishes no numbers. Third-party catalogue figures (161 cm, 64 kg, 28 DoF, 2 kg arm payload, 3 m/s) were not filled.

name: Linglong L2.0
summary: Linglong L2.0, the firefighting configuration of the Shanghai humanoid innovation center's biped platform.
note: No maker product page or datasheet for L2.0 was found (the center's WRC 2026 entry lists Linglong L1 and H1 only; checked 2026-11-17), so spec fields stay empty. Press coverage of WRC 2026 and of the 2026 Yizhuang half-marathon reports L2.0 as a firefighting humanoid: 173 cm, 42 active DoF, up to 3 m/s, 560 TOPS edge compute, >95% domestic hardware, heat-resistant suit, RISC-V K3 AI CPU with the OpenLoong control framework. Those figures are press-reported, not maker-published.

name: North
summary: Sharpa's first full-body humanoid, a 67-DOF robot shown at CES 2026 running autonomous ping-pong, card dealing and a 30+ step assembly for four days straight.
note: Maker pages give only the 67-DOF total and the demonstrated capabilities: fully autonomous manipulation over four consecutive 8-hour days at CES 2026, ping-pong rallies with <0.02 s hand response, a 30+ step paper-windmill assembly, card dealing from a full deck with vision-language input, and camera use with ~2 mm finger positioning. The hand is the Sharpa Wave, 22 active DOF with sub-millimetre tactile resolution. Height, weight, payload, speed, battery, runtime, compute and price are not published, so those fields stay empty; the page is an enquiry form only ('Enquire about North').

name: T1
summary: Bipedal humanoid from Sichuan TLIBOT with 41 body DoF and a 1110 Wh battery, rated to carry 10 kg in its arms and over 100 kg in a deep squat.

Height and walking speed are not published on the maker page.

name: Simbot

The maker does not publish a product name (the catalog and WRC exhibitor record use 'Simbot'), and height, weight, speed, battery, runtime and price are not published, so those fields stay empty. Target settings are hotels, homes, senior care and retail; no customer deployment has been named.

name: i7 Pro
onboard_compute: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16GB (standard) / NVIDIA DRIVE Thor-U (Pro)
summary: Simplexity Robotics' i7 Pro wheeled humanoid for retail and logistics sorting: 18 active DOF excluding hands, a 650 mm lifting column, two 1,650 Wh batteries and the SimpleWAM world-action model.

name: Xiaoxin

note: No maker website or datasheet was found. The only company-supplied source is Sinovai Robotics' own WRC 2026 exhibitor entry: 44 DOF, 7-axis arms, operating height above 2 m, an 11-DOF 'elf hand', squatting and lifting motion, a large-model voice system with second-level response, and uses in cultural-tourism guiding, commercial service, research and education, and corporate reception. Press reports place Xiaoxin at the Chengdu Natural History Museum from December 2025 and in service as a qualified guide from February 2026, hence Pilot. Height, weight, payload, speed, battery and runtime are not published. Left as unconfirmed because the maker has no verifiable product page and the figures come from an exhibitor submission, not a maker datasheet.

note: Maker datasheet (DARWIN-01, distributed also by its Japanese partner): 680 x 640 x 1,736 mm standing (1,142 mm squatting, 859 mm folded), 200 kg body weight, 10 kg rated payload with a dexterous hand (5 kg with an industrial gripper), 23+ DOF including end effectors (chassis 3, waist 4, 7 per arm, head 2), 0-1,900 mm working range, 1.5 m/s maximum speed with omnidirectional drive, +/-10 mm and +/-1-degree docking accuracy, 48 V 30 Ah battery (=1,440 Wh, derived; the maker states only 48 V 30 Ah) for 6 h and 0.5 h charge to 80% DOD, 0-50 C, dual diagonal 2D LiDAR with optional 3D LiDAR plus depth camera and 360-degree aerial and floor obstacle avoidance, Wi-Fi and 5G, VR teleoperation for data collection. Launched 2025 and shown at WAIC 2025 with Mech-Mind picking software. Standard Robots' own product page lists only the OASIS mobile platforms, so the datasheet PDF is the maker spec source.

name: Flex

note: Maker page: 5 ft 9 in (about 1,753 mm) foldable wheeled humanoid for evaluation in restaurants, hospitality and retail; released/announced September 2026, with 'availability and final specifications to be announced'. Weight, DOF, payload, speed, battery, runtime and price are not published, so those fields stay empty.

name: Nova

note: Maker page and its specification sheet (a Nova reference configuration): 5 ft (about 152 cm), 70 lb (31.8 kg), wheeled differential drive with zero-radius turning, 0.8-1.2 m/s (1.2 m/s entered as the upper bound), 2-3 kg arm payload (3 kg entered), depth cameras plus RGB camera and IMU, on-device LLM with cloud fallback, voice interaction in English/Spanish/Italian, interactive touchscreen, target runtime up to 10-12 h configuration-dependent (11 h entered as the midpoint), 3 h charge, indoor commercial spaces, Wi-Fi with OTA updates and a monitoring dashboard. Launched December 2025 when the company moved from bipedal testing to a wheeled base with two 7-DOF arms. DOF total, battery capacity and price are not stated.

name: Phi-Bot X1

note: Maker site (Sunrising AI / 光象科技, Tsinghua-incubated, founded 2025-04; released Phi-Bot X1 on 2026-06-10): 27 whole-body DOF with 1 kHz whole-joint control, 6 kg single-arm payload, 0-2.5 m working range, four-swerve-wheel omnidirectional chassis with active steering, crab and diagonal motion and in-place turning, 10 mm positioning and 0.05 mm end-effector repeatability, perception with 3 LiDAR, 3 RGBD (up to 5), 1 binocular camera and 8 ultrasonic radars, dual batteries with 1-minute hot-swap, quick-change end effectors. Height, weight, speed, battery capacity and runtime are not published. Maker reports real line deployment at premium car makers (welding load/unload, mobile inspection) and ISO 9001/45001/14001 certification from TUV Rheinland.

name: SYNDA R1
summary: SYNDA R1 is Shanghai STEP Electric's first industrial-grade embodied humanoid, launched in December 2025 as a full-size bipedal-style platform for factory work.

The release carries the specification table only as an image, so no height, weight, DOF, payload, speed or battery figure could be read from a maker source and every spec field is left empty. STEP (新时达, Shanghai STEP Electric, 002527) is an industrial robot and motion-control company; the humanoid line targets its own manufacturing scenarios first.

Height, weight and price are not published. STEP's corporate site carries the R1 launch release but no R2 datasheet, so the WRC entry is the maker-side spec source.

Speed, battery and runtime are not published. Status is Prototype: it was exhibited and is being tested in the company's own lines and in a government project with a display maker and KAIST through 2030.

Speed, payload, battery, runtime and price are not published.

Vbot's site (vbot.cn) currently profiles its robot dog and the ATOM page is not public, so the launch figures are recorded here and weight, speed, payload, runtime and price are left empty (catalogue figures such as 50 kg, 4 km/h, 6 kg and USD 25,000 are not maker values).

Whole-body carrying capacity, battery capacity in Wh and price are not published.

name: SA02

summary: EngineAI's low-cost companion humanoid for young buyers, previewed at the 2025 World Robot Conference at CNY 38,500 and not yet on sale.
note: EngineAI's own news page (10 Aug 2025) previews SA02 as 'Everyone's First Humanoid Robot' starting at CNY 38,500 (about USD 5,300) at the 2025 World Robot Conference. EngineAI has no SA02 product page (its current product line is PM01, T800, JS01, SE01 and S2), and the 1 .25 m / 25 kg build and DoF count come only from the launch spec sheet as reproduced in trade press, which quotes both 26 and 28 DoF - so dof is left empty and the conflicting counts noted. Payload, speed, runtime and battery are not published.

name: Dora
summary: Noetix's compact service humanoid from 2024, later folded into the E1 line; the maker no longer documents it.
note: Noetix no longer lists Dora: its founder said in a March 2025 interview that Dora became the E1 after the tooling was consolidated, and the maker's current catalogue has no Dora page (checked 2026-11-17). Third-party figures (100 cm, 20 kg, 20 DoF) are not used.

name: K1
onboard_compute: JAKA RoboHub controller (Intel Core i3/i5/i7 12th-13th gen, optional NVIDIA RTX 3050)
summary: JAKA's K1 seven-axis dual-arm platform for dual-arm assembly and embodied-AI data collection.
note: Maker hardware manual (JAKA K1, V01): a 7-axis dual-arm collaborative platform - per arm 5 kg payload, 14 kg mass, 976 mm working radius, repeatability +/-0.05 mm, TCP max 1 m/s, 48 V DC supply, RoboHub controller with Intel Core i12/i13 CPU, EtherCAT. Dual-arm synchronised control (SyncPath, SyncForce, SyncCalib, SelfAware). DoF field left empty because the maker states 7 axes per arm, not a whole-body count; no height, weight or runtime for a complete robot is published. SCOPE: K1 has no mobile base - it is a bench-mounted dual-arm platform, which AGENTS.md section 3 excludes as arms/cobots; kept here unchanged (no deletion) and flagged for an owner scope decision. The wheeled K1W and legged K1L are separate models.

name: Atlas (hydraulic, 2013)
summary: The original hydraulic Atlas that Boston Dynamics built for DARPA's Robotics Challenge in 2013, retired in April 2024 when the electric Atlas replaced it.
note: Built by Boston Dynamics for DARPA and unveiled 11 Jul 2013; the figures come from the commissioning agency's release (darpa.mil/news/2013/atlas-robot-unveiled): 6 ft 2 in (1.88 m), 330 lb (150 kg), 28 hydraulically actuated joints, a Carnegie Robotics sensor head with LIDAR and stereo sensors, an on-board real-time control computer, a hydraulic pump with thermal management, and two hand sets (iRobot, Sandia). It ran tethered to off-board power and computing in the 2013 DRC Trials; DARPA's own timeline records the mid-2015 rebuild to on-board power. Boston Dynamics has no current product page for this generation. Marked Discontinued because Boston Dynamics announced the retirement of the hydraulic Atlas on 17 Apr 2024 with the 'Introducing Electric Atlas' post. Runtime, speed and payload are not published by the maker and stay empty.

name: L1
summary: Wheeled-legged industrial humanoid from Moon Dynamics announced in June 2026 for heavy material handling; no maker page or confirmed specification exists.
note: No maker page found (checked 2026-11-17): Moon Dynamics (揽月动力) appears only through press coverage and third-party catalogues, and no official site lists L1. Press figures are 165 cm, 60 kg, 25 kg payload, 7 km/h, 3 h, wheeled-legged; none is confirmed by a maker source, so no field is filled.

name: PrimeBOT T1
compute_detail: 8-core high-performance processor + Orin Nano
summary: PrimeBOT's transformable personal robot: walks as a wheel-legged humanoid indoors and switches to quadruped form outdoors for grass, slopes and stairs.
note: Maker (启元机器人 / PrimeBOT, Shanghai; STAR Market 688585) spec page: 100 cm tall, ~16.3 kg with battery (T1) / ~16.8 kg (T1 Pro), payload <=3 kg, 3 m/s in quadruped form and 2.5 m/s in wheel-legged form, 2x ToF + monocular camera (T1) or 5x ToF + stereo (T1 Pro), 2 fisheye cameras, 360-degree coverage, 15 cm obstacle crossing, 30-degree slope, 10 km/h running (OTA), voice-guided stair following, auto-docking (accessory). Battery capacity, runtime and DOF count are not published. SCOPE FLAG: sold as a consumer personal/companion and education robot ('global first transformable personal robot'); form factor is wheel-legged/quadruped, not a bipedal humanoid.

name: Xiao Liu
summary: Wheeled demonstration humanoid from Tencent Robotics X Lab and the successor to Xiao Wu, built for eldercare and home assistance with cable-tendon arms and three-fingered hands; it gave a therapeutic-massage demonstration at WAIC 2026.
note: Xiao Liu was shown at WAIC on 2026-07-17 and is described by Tencent as a demonstrative robot; the maker says technical parameters, further demonstrations and commercialisation plans are not yet disclosed, and its WAIC release covers models and platforms only. Dimensions, weight, DoF, payload, runtime and price are therefore empty; catalogue figures (165 cm, 70 kg, 38 DoF, USD 90,000) are not maker figures.

name: Nori L3
summary: Pre-release name of Nori's sub-$2,000 home robot, announced in July 2026 and now sold as the A3.
note: No maker page for L3 (checked 2026-11-17): Nori now sells the same $1,688 robot as the A3. L3 figures (20 DoF, 1 kg per arm, sub-$2,000) appear only in the founder's 2026-07-28 post announcing pre-orders, and L2 buyers were offered free upgrades to it, so L3 is treated as the earlier name of A3 rather than a separately documented model.

name: Asimov 2
summary: Announced successor to Menlo's open-source Asimov 1; Menlo has published no specifications or shipping date yet.
note: Menlo's own documentation page for Asimov 2 (checked 2026-11-17) says the page holds V2 concepts only and that full specs and the shipping date are unknown, so no specification can be recorded. Announced as the successor to Asimov 1.

name: K0
sdk_name: Open-source stack: hardware BoM, STEP CAD, source code, simulation assets, tutorials (ROS 2)
summary: K0 is the first open-source humanoid of ROBOTIS' AI Sapiens line: a 1.3 m, 23-DOF platform on in-house DYNAMIXEL-Q quasi-direct-drive actuators for learning-based locomotion and manipulation.
note: Maker page: 1,300 mm height, 34 kg, 23 DOF (5 per arm, 6 per leg, 1 waist), max arm payload 3 kg, DYNAMIXEL Q actuators (QM-060 x 14, QM-080 x 9), Jetson Orin NX 16GB (up to 100 sparse INT8 TOPS), 46.8 V 9,000 mAh battery (=421.2 Wh, derived from V x Ah), Wi-Fi 5 + Bluetooth 5.0, 2 Ethernet, USB 2.0 x 2 and USB 3.0 x 2, 24 V/10 A and 12 V/10 A power outputs. Sold as a development platform, not a finished product: DYNAMIXEL-Q and the open-source release (BoM, STEP files, code, simulation, tutorials) were still being rolled out, so status is Announced. Max speed, runtime and a sensor list are not published.

name: Walden
summary: Wheeled dual-arm robot from Walden Robotics (a Toyota Research Institute spin-out) doing machine tending, tool setting, parts kitting and assembly in production, including at a Toyota plant in North America.
note: Walden publishes no hardware specifications (checked 2026-11-17): its site describes a wheeled or fixed base with a humanoid upper body, two arms and a sensor head, running its Large Behavior Models (LBM 2.0, 'Sage') with remote assistance, and reports production work at a Toyota plant since February 2026. Height, weight, DoF, payload, speed, runtime and price therefore stay empty; catalogue figures such as 165 cm, 90 kg, 24 DoF or USD 120,000 are not maker values.

name: LightBot-0
compute_detail: 7-25 W edge module, 67 INT8 TOPS
sensors: Chest-mounted Intel RealSense D435 depth camera
summary: Light Origins' custom 90 cm research humanoid, 18.9 kg with 21 actuated joints, used to demonstrate onboard perceptive parkour with a single policy.
note: Light Origins describes Lightbot 0 as its custom 90 cm, 18.9 kg humanoid with 21 actuated joints (research paper and blog, checked 2026-11-17). No price, payload, speed or runtime is published and the products page still says the bipedal humanoid is coming, so this is a research prototype.

name: P0
summary: Pink Robotics' German-built prototype P0: 1.75 m, 82 kg, 32 DoF and 8 kg payload, aimed at parcel sorting in distribution centres.
note: Pink Robotics (Anyscrew GmbH) site (checked 2026-11-17): 1.75 m, 82 kg, 32-DoF motion system, 8 kg payload, German-built prototype for parcel sorting. Speed, runtime, sensing and price are not published; demonstrations are teleoperated.

name: D01
sensors: Whole-body tactile E-skin (0.1-20 N per taxel, 0.2 N resolution, 10 mm spatial resolution, 100 Hz)
summary: Sharpa's D01 dexterous upper-body humanoid: 66 DOF with Wave hands, 7-DOF arms and whole-body tactile E-skin, built for manipulation research and teleoperation data collection.
note: Maker spec sheet: height 1,109-1,624 mm depending on folding (1,624 mm standing entered here), 495 mm wide x 594 mm long, about 40 kg WITHOUT the chassis, 66 DOF with hands (head 3, arms 7 x 2, Wave hands 22 x 2, torso 5 - no leg or wheel DOF appear in the total), dual-arm span 1,900 mm, rated 5 kg payload per arm, end-effector speed >10.5 m/s, +/-0.2 mm repeatability, up to 1,000 Hz control, 1000BASE-T Ethernet and Wi-Fi 6, Jetson Thor with 128 GB LPDDR5X, head stereo camera and wrist fisheye cameras, body tactile E-skin. Announced at IROS 2026 (2026-09-28, PR Newswire). Locomotion left empty because the maker lists no leg or drive DOF for D01 and its weight is quoted without a chassis; battery, runtime and price are not published.

name: Nadia
summary: IHMC's full-size research humanoid with hybrid hydraulic-electric actuation and one of the widest ranges of motion of its generation, built with Boardwalk Robotics.
note: Maker pages (IHMC Robotics humanoid design; Boardwalk Robotics Nadia): 29 joints with unusually large range of motion, hybrid actuation (Moog hydraulic Integrated Smart Actuators in legs and spine, electric actuators at hip/spine yaw and in the arms), carbon-fibre exoskeleton, VR teleoperation, IHMC whole-body control software; funded by ONR, ARL, NASA JSC and TARDEC. Height, mass, speed and runtime are not published by IHMC (190 cm / 100 kg / 3.5 km/h appear only in third-party catalogues and were not filled). No price.

name: Vesoma Gen 1
summary: Vesoma's first bipedal humanoid, built as one system with a self-improving reinforcement-learning agent that acquires locomotion and manipulation from its own interaction, for manufacturing, logistics and warehousing.
note: Vesoma publishes no dimensions, weight, DoF, payload, battery, runtime or price: its site shows Vesoma 1 only as a design visualisation marked 'under development', while alpha prototypes walk in the lab on a self-learned policy, and the company's launch note describes a six-month build from design to walking. Those fields are left empty rather than filled from catalogues.

name: Tau Humanoid
summary: Humanoid that cleans homes and offices as an invite-only service in San Francisco, working with a human supervisor rather than being sold as a product.
note: Tau Robotics publishes no hardware specifications: its site describes the robots only as humanoids with 3D-printed claw hands and antennae heads that work alongside a supervising human, able to walk stairs and use elevators (checked 2026-11-17). Press reports describe the body as a modified Unitree G1 with Tau's own cameras, grippers and compute, but the maker does not state this. Per-unit price, height, weight, payload, speed, battery and runtime are therefore left empty; the ~USD 55,000 and 132 cm / 35 kg figures in catalogues are not maker figures.

name: Astra
price_note: from USD 9,999 standard price; reservation with a USD 200 deposit (maker, checked 2026-11-17)
summary: StarBot Astra is a 5 ft, 23-DOF humanoid research platform from StarBot USA for motion control, reinforcement learning and sim-to-real work, sold by reservation from USD 9,999.
note: Maker page: 5 ft (about 152 cm), 75 lb (about 34 kg), 23 full-body DOF, 48 V battery, 2-5 h runtime (3.5 h entered as the midpoint; the maker does not say which end matches which condition), 1 h charge, from USD 9,999 with a USD 200 reservation deposit, released July 2026 and listed with an Isaac Simulation label. Payload, DOF breakdown, sensors, compute, SDK and locomotion type are not stated for Astra (the homepage's detailed spec sheet is labelled a Nova reference configuration and was not applied to Astra), so locomotion is left empty rather than assumed wheeled. Deliveries are not confirmed: availability and schedule are confirmed in the purchase agreement.

name: Laborer M1
summary: Glroad's heavy-load biped industrial humanoid (1.87 m, 86 kg) with a 50 kg dual-arm rating, billed as the industry's first 50 kg-class humanoid.
note: Maker parameter table (glroad.com, 劳动者M1): height 187 cm, mass 86 kg, dual-arm payload 50 kg (combined, test conditions not stated), moving speed >1.2 m/s (field = 1.2 m/s, lower bound), battery 22 Ah (voltage not published), runtime 2 h, 27 whole-body DoF (6 per leg, 1 head; the table's single-arm figure is inconsistent with the maker's own diagram showing 7-DoF arms), peak joint torque 430 N.m, dual encoders, arm-end accuracy printed illegibly on the page. Released 20 Aug 2026 with the C1. C1 is a different, much smaller robot.

name: Laborer C1
compute_detail: 100 TOPS / 157 TOPS
summary: Glroad's compact biped service humanoid (1.37 m, 21 DoF, 38 kg) for store guidance, reception and exhibition hosting.
note: Maker parameter table (glroad.com, 劳动者C1): height 137.1 cm, mass 38 kg, arm length 57.9 cm, moving speed >2 m/s (field = 2 m/s, lower bound), operating -20 to 60 C, battery 10 Ah (voltage not published, so Wh left empty), runtime 2 h walking / 4 h standing, 21 whole-body DoF (6 per leg, 1 waist, 4 per arm expandable), peak joint torque 150 N.m, dual encoders, gear ratio 25, Orin NX 100T/157T, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.2, 4G/5G, Type-C/Ethernet, handheld remote, secondary development supported. Released 20 Aug 2026 with the M1.

name: Y2-B
compute_detail: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16GB + 512GB SSD
sensors: LiDAR for autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance
summary: Wheeled dual-arm robot (Y2-B) from Sichuan TLIBOT with pitching arms and a 2194 mm working range, for picking, handling and data collection.
note: Maker figures: 745x525x1341 mm folded (the folded height is recorded above; no extended height is given), <=85 kg, 2194 mm working range, 5 kg rated per arm, <=1.2 m/s, slope <=5 deg, 20 mm obstacles and gaps, pivot turn, LiDAR navigation to +/-50 mm and +/-3 deg, 4 h runtime, 3.5 h charge, Jetson Orin NX 16G with 512 GB SSD, ROS 2 and API.

name: Y4
summary: Fixed-base dual-arm data-collection robot (Y4) from Sichuan TLIBOT with a 653 mm working range and 30 Hz teleoperation for industrial and embodied-AI teaching.
note: Maker selection guide: fixed base with no chassis (so no locomotion is recorded and no battery runtime is quoted), 1445 mm tall, <=55 kg, dual arms, 653 mm working range, ROS 2 and API. The maker's Y4 product note adds 30 Hz high-frequency teleoperation support for data collection.

name: Atlas on Wheels
summary: A one-off experiment in which Boston Dynamics swapped the electric Atlas' feet for scooter wheels to stress-test its actuators and whole-body RL control.
note: Maker blog post 'Atlas On a Roll' by Atlas controls engineer Xiaoyu (Andy) Wu, published with a video on 9 Nov 2026: the feet of an electric Atlas were replaced by off-the-shelf scooter rims on the existing ankle actuators, with a single custom adapter as the only new part, and driven by a whole-body reinforcement-learning policy trained in simulation. Boston Dynamics states plainly that 'a wheeled Atlas isn't a product. It's a research testbed', announces no price or date, and says the insights are being fed back into the standard legged Atlas. Because the wheels sit on the legs in place of feet, locomotion recorded as Wheel-legged (the seed value was Wheeled). Maker publishes no height, weight, speed or payload for this configuration, so all spec fields stay empty.

name: Agile ONE S
compute_detail: NVIDIA Jetson Thor + Intel Core i3 N305 base computing module
summary: Open reference humanoid platform with onboard Jetson Thor compute and a choice of four-finger or two-finger hands.
note: Maker page gives no height, weight or speed. Hand options: four-finger 9 DoF hand or 1 DoF two-finger gripper.

name: ALICE 3
compute_detail: NUC11TNKi7; Jetson AGX Xavier
summary: Korean research humanoid with human-like proportions: 144 cm, 27.5 kg, 27 DoF.
note: Maker spec box: 144 cm / 27.5 kg; 27 DoF = leg 6x2, waist 1, arm 7x2, head 2; says specs vary with options.

name: XTRON T170A
summary: Bipedal humanoid research platform from Foxtech.
note: Maker page: each arm carries up to 5 kg. No other figures were extracted from the page text, so the remaining fields stay empty.

name: RoXi
summary: Bosch Rexroth's mobile humanoid demonstrator: a wheeled mobile platform from its ctrlX AUTOMATION "Mobile Robots" set carrying two Kassow Robots 7-axis cobots, shown tending machines and handling parts.
note: Maker sources checked 2026-11-28: Bosch Rexroth's press release PI 044/26 (3 Nov 2026) and the ctrlX AUTOMATION story present RoXi as a demonstrator of the solution set for mobile humanoid robotics, combining a mobile platform (controls, I/O modules, laser-based localisation software) with Kassow Robots 7-axis cobots, including dual-arm configurations; live at SPS 2026, Nuremberg, Hall 7 booth 450, 24-26 Nov 2026. It is a showcase rather than a catalogued product: no dimensions, payload, speed, battery, runtime or price are published, so every spec field stays empty. Not listed by any competitor catalog consulted.

name: Kargo50
compute_detail: Control cabinet: Intel Core Ultra 7 255H, 32 GB RAM, 96 TOPS, EtherCAT
summary: JAKA's heavy-duty wheeled humanoid: two 7-DoF arms rated 25 kg each and 50 kg together on a lifting, pitching body, for heavy tote handling and machine tending.
note: Maker product page (zh) checked 2026-11-28: two 7-DoF humanoid arms, 25 kg rated per arm and 50 kg for both arms together, 850 mm working radius, 1.51 m/s typical tool-tip speed, 320 kg net machine weight, head pitch -20 to 45 deg, neck rotation +/-90 deg, body pitch 0 to 90 deg, lift stroke 0-780 mm, two lithium-iron-phosphate batteries, one obstacle-avoidance sensor and an emergency-stop button, EtherCAT, 48 V DC (30-60 V). The page's physical table is headed 'control cabinet': IP20, 178 x 178 x 170 mm, 2,000 W average / 4,000 W peak, Intel Core Ultra 7 255H, 96 TOPS, 32 GB RAM, USB x3 and RJ45 x2 belong to the cabinet, so ip_rating and the compute fields carry that qualifier. Overall robot height, length, width, drive speed, battery capacity and runtime are not published and stay empty; total DoF is not stated (only 7 per arm is). Unveiled at CIIF 2026 (Shanghai, 12-16 Oct 2026) together with the Zu50 cobot per JAKA's own announcement; the page does not state a release year. The English page exists but renders no spec text, so the Chinese page is the source.
